items: Select a block in the hotbar with keys 1 to 0, or pick it from the Build catalog in creative.
Aim at the face where you want the block. A ghost shows the cell it will fill.
Right-click to place one block. The held item must be a block. With a bow, rifle or throwing rock in hand, right-click aims or throws instead.

blocks.text: A whole block is eight half-metre pieces. In survival, each whole block uses 8 pieces of that material from your pack, and the game says so if you are short. Creative placement is free. {{whole-block-placement}}
If any part of the target cell is occupied, the whole block is refused and the outline turns red. You cannot place a block inside yourself. Plants and water in the target cell are overwritten.

In creative, middle-click the block you aim at to pick it. If the block is already in a hotbar slot, that slot is selected. Otherwise the block is held without changing your other slots. Aiming at a door picks the closed door. Middle-click does nothing in survival. {{middle-click-pick}}

Your aim passes through water to the first solid block. Stand on the shore and aim at a lake or sea bed, then build up from it. You cannot click the water surface itself. Placed blocks replace water and plants in their cell. {{building-in-water}}
A block is refused, with a message in the status line, when:

items: For ordinary block placement, select a block. Furniture, doors and chests have their own placement steps below.
Your hands are empty, or a tool, bow, rifle or throwing rock is in hand.
A solid block is in the target cell.
In survival, your pack does not have 8 pieces of the material for a whole block.
The world already holds 200,000 changed blocks. New building is refused, and the save warns before the limit. {{placement-restrictions}}

blocks.text: The Water block in the creative catalog is a flowing source. Right-click with Water selected to place one. It spreads up to 7 half-metre cells sideways and pours down over edges. Flowing water does not go away on its own. {{flowing-water}}

items: Placing a block into water replaces that water cell.
Digging next to the sea or a lake lets water flow into the new gap.
Survival players cannot pick up or place water. There are no buckets.
The other five water types are blocks. They do not flow.

blocks.text: To stop unwanted flowing water, fill each wet cell with blocks. On a multiplayer server the server runs the water.

Hold [[Shift]] to place or mine one half-metre piece instead of a whole cube. In creative, press [[N]] to toggle detail size without holding Shift; press N again for whole blocks. This lets you keep flying level while building small details. {{half-metre-detail-building}}

rows: Carve one half-metre piece from a block. Logs and cactus still fell the whole tree or stem.
Clean view. Hides the outline, ghost and HUD while you play.

blocks.text: Holding Shift also sneaks on foot, dives in water and descends while flying.

Doors are built from boards. They come in three styles and two sizes. A small door is one metre wide and two metres tall, with one leaf. A wide door is two metres wide and three metres tall, with two one-metre leaves. {{doors}}
Choose a door to craft

Open [[E]] > Craft and select any door recipe in the Timber section. Three buttons appear above the preview: **Style**, **Wood** and **Size**. Click one, or move keyboard focus to it and press [[Enter]], to step to its next choice. The other two choices stay as they are. {{door-styles-and-moves}}

items: **Style:** Plain, Panelled or Windowed. Panelled doors have framed, recessed panels. Windowed doors have glass panes in the upper part.
**Wood:** Alder, Birch, Pine, Oak, Fruitwood, Acacia, Willow, Mangrove, Jungle, Cherry, Giant, Palm, Mesquite, Fig or Cypress. A door of a named wood needs boards of exactly that wood.
**Any boards** is the original Wooden door. It takes boards of any wood, mixed if you like, and comes in Plain only. The Style button is greyed out until you choose a wood.
**Size:** 1 x 2 m for one leaf, or 2 x 3 m for two leaves.

Changing a choice only selects a different recipe. Doors you carry or have hung, and crafts already queued, stay as they are. If a recipe filter would hide your choice, the filter turns off and the status line says "Showing all recipes".

blocks.text: Costs are the same for every wood:

items: **Plain or Panelled, 1 x 2 m:** one block of boards (8 half-metre pieces).
**Plain or Panelled, 2 x 3 m:** two blocks of boards (16 pieces).
**Windowed, 1 x 2 m:** 6 board pieces and 2 glass pieces.
**Windowed, 2 x 3 m:** 12 board pieces and 4 glass pieces.

blocks.text: Recipe names follow your choices, for example Oak door, Wide panelled oak door or Windowed birch door. The original two are Wooden door and Wide wooden door.
Hang, open and take down

items: Hold the door and right click solid ground to hang it. The spot needs free space and solid ground under it. A player or animal standing where the leaves would go also stops the hang.
Right click a hung door to open it, and right click again to close it. A door swings away from the player who opens it, from either side. It has its own opening and closing sound.

The leaves turn on their hinges over 0.35 seconds, easing in and settling gently. If the leaves are not drawn on screen yet, for example while the chunk is still being rebuilt, the swing waits up to one second; a wide door across a chunk edge then turns both halves together. Using a door again while it is moving turns it back from where it stands.
A door will not open if anything other than air, water or plants is in its swing path. It also will not open while you or an animal stands where the leaves sweep. Clear the space and try again.

An open leaf stands a metre out of the doorway. You and walking animals cannot walk through it, and you cannot place a block into the space it stands in. Undo and redo refuse a change to that space too.
You cannot close a door while you stand in its opening. Step out first. A door will not shut while an animal stands in its opening.

Mine any leaf to take the whole door down; in Survival, hold left click until it comes down. In Survival the door goes back into your pack if there is room; if the pack is full, it is left hanging. Mining a block next to an open leaf leaves the door standing.
In Creative, middle click a door to hold one of the same style, wood and size. This works on either leaf, and on an open door.

blocks.text: Move a door (Creative)

items: Close the door and wait for it to stop swinging. Put tools away and use ordinary block building, not a brush.
Aim at the door and press [[Shift]] + left click. A blue outline marks the original door, which stays where it is for now.
Aim at clear, solid ground. The ghost shows where the door will stand. Press [[R]] to give it a quarter turn.
Right click to move the door. The status line says "Moved door | Ctrl+Z undoes".
To cancel, left click or press [[B]]. The original door is left as it was.

blocks.text: [[Ctrl+Z]] puts a moved door back and [[Ctrl+Shift+Z]] moves it again. Finish or cancel a move before you undo.

The new spot must be empty air, with no water or plants, and every leaf needs solid ground under it. You must move or turn the door, and nobody may stand where it will go. If the status line says "Move only a complete closed door after it stops swinging", close the door, wait and try again. Undo and Redo are refused if the door or its space has changed since.

On a server, doors can be hung, opened and taken down once the server accepts the action. In Survival, hanging spends one matching door after the server confirms, and taking one down returns the matching door. In Creative on a server, door moves, Undo and Redo work too: each step waits for the server to confirm, and a move waits while another server action is unfinished. A door move from before you respawned cannot be undone. Blueprints skip door leaves, so a door is not copied.
A wooden chest is one metre cube of storage. It keeps items where you set it down, so you can leave things at a build site. {{wooden-chests}}

items: **Wooden chest:** one block of boards of any wood. Craft it in the Timber section.
Hold the chest and right click to set it down. It fills the metre cell under the ghost, with the latch toward you.
Right click a chest within 6 m to open its Chest tab. Your pack and the chest sit side by side. The lid makes an opening sound, and a closing sound when the Chest tab shuts or you walk out of reach.
Click an item to move one across. Shift+click moves as much of that item as fits.
A chest holds up to 250 kg and up to 64 kinds of item. A world holds at most 512 chests.
To take a chest up, mine it. In Survival it goes back into your pack with everything inside, but only if the pack has room for all of it. In Creative, empty it first; you get no chest item back.

blocks.text: Refinish a chest
You can give a placed chest new woods for its body, lid and fittings. Its contents stay inside. {{chest-refinishing}}

items: Equip the Furniture hammer, aim at a placed chest within 6 m, and press [[E]] or right click.
The Refinish chest panel opens in the Build tab, starting with oak. Use the **Body**, **Lid** and **Fittings** buttons to choose each wood. Any of the fifteen woods works.
Press **Apply changes**. **Cancel**, or closing the panel, keeps the original chest as it was.

blocks.text: In Survival, refinishing costs 4 boards of the body wood, 3 of the lid wood and 1 of the fittings wood: one block of boards when all three match. The old chest supplies the box. Creative is free.

[[Ctrl+Z]] turns it back into the original chest with the same contents and, in Survival, returns the boards. [[Ctrl+Shift+Z]] applies the finish again. Both need the same game mode, with the contents and woods as they were right after the change. In Survival, Undo needs room in your pack for the boards, and Redo needs the boards again.

A refinished chest is storage furniture. Right click opens it, and it holds up to 250 kg and 64 kinds of item. Empty it before taking it up. Taking up one refinished in Survival returns the chest and its boards. The **Chest** plan in the carpentry workbench (the Wooden chest plan) makes the same kind of chest from one you carry: in Survival it costs one Wooden chest plus the same boards, and Creative is free.

On a server, wait for the server to confirm each chest action. You can set chests down, open them, move items and refinish them in Survival or Creative. In Survival, hold left click to take a chest up with its contents, if your pack has room. In Creative, empty it first; taking it up gives no chest item. On a server, a refinish from before you respawned or reconnected cannot be undone. Blasts, tracks, brushes, copy and blueprints leave chest cells alone.

Chairs, tables, desks, sofas, kitchen units, bathroom fixtures, storage furniture, beds and lamps are built from reusable furniture plans. In Survival, carry a **Furniture hammer** from E > Craft > Tools & arms; in Creative, pick a plan in the Build catalogue. Survival pays for the chosen materials when you place a piece. Plans, materials, moving, table joins and lanterns on tables are explained in {{guide:furniture-and-carpentry|Furniture and carpentry}}.

In creative mode, press B to move to the next brush. The order is Block, Line, Wall, Floor, Replace, Copy, Blueprint, Bench, Railing and Roof. You can also pick a brush from the E > Build tab. {{creative-brush-cycle}}

items: Block: Right-click to place one block.
Line: Right-click once to set the first corner, aim at the far end and right-click again. The line follows the longer direction. {{brush-line-wall-floor}}
Wall: Same two clicks. The wall stands upright along the longer horizontal direction.
Floor: Same two clicks. The floor stays level at the height of the first corner.
Replace: Aim at a block of the material to swap and right-click. Aim at the opposite corner and right-click again. Matching blocks in the box become the block in your hand. {{brush-replace}}

Copy: Right-click two opposite corners to copy every block in that box except air and the Camp crate. Water and plants are copied too. Right-click again to paste at the ghost. R turns the paste 90 degrees. B discards the copy. {{brush-copy-paste}}
Blueprint: Save a build, then place it again. See the Blueprints section. {{creative-blueprints}}
Bench, Railing, Roof: One right-click stamps a fixed shape at the ghost. Press R first to turn it 90 degrees. {{brush-bench-railing-roof}}

blocks.text: Every brush except Block shows a ghost first. One action changes at most 512 half-metre pieces (64 whole blocks). Blueprints have their own limits. If a cell holds a solid block, nothing is built. Water and plants do not block a build. Replace is the exception: it swaps only the material you aim at. Hold Shift on the first click for half-metre steps.
Pressing B clears a corner selection or a copied selection. Copies are lost when you change brush or leave the world.
A blueprint is a build you save and place again. In creative mode it is free to place. In survival, placing it uses pieces from your pack. Blueprints do not work on servers yet.
Save a blueprint (creative)

items: Press [[B]] until the brush says **Blueprint**. You can also pick it in **E > Build**.
Aim at a ground corner of the build and press [[Shift]] + right-click. The status says **First corner set**.

Aim at the opposite ground corner and press [[Shift]] + right-click again. The **Structures** panel opens with a picture of what was taken. Nothing is saved yet. Until then, each corner you marked shows a post, and the box that would be saved is outlined. To cancel, press [[Shift]] + right-click on the same corner again.
Type a name and press **Save**. A name that is taken needs a second press to replace it. **Keep both** saves a copy called Name 2. Closing the panel discards the capture.
If you just placed a saved blueprint, its name is filled in and the panel says **Enter updates it**. Press **Enter**, then **Enter** again, to replace that file. Type another name to keep both.
Aim where you want it. The ghost shows the result. Right-click to build it. The whole build is one undo step, so [[Ctrl]]+[[Z]] removes it.

blocks.text: Build a blueprint in survival

items: Press [[B]] to take the Blueprint tool out. Press [[B]] again to put it away. In survival it is the only build tool, so [[B]] is the only key you need.
Aim where you want the build. The ghost turns red when you lack pieces.
Check the list on screen. It shows each material as carried / needed.
Right-click to build. The build is paid for in one go, or refused whole.

blocks.text: Each half-metre piece you change costs one piece of the item that block drops when mined. A whole block is 8 pieces. Dirt-type turf costs dirt. Voxels that already hold the right block cost nothing. If you lack any material, nothing is built or spent, and the status names the missing items.

rows: Lift the ghost 1 m up or down.
Delete the selected blueprint and its file.

blocks.text: The save leaves out water, cells you carved out of the terrain and the Camp crate. The status line says how many. A blueprint can be up to 128 m along any side and you can keep up to 64. Placement is refused if it would build over blocks you placed yourself or the Camp crate, or on top of you. Step back and try again.

Saved blueprints are plain files with the `.blueprint` extension in a folder named `blueprints`. The game looks for that folder where it starts. Without it, blueprints last only until you leave the session.
Structure workshop

The Structure workshop is a flat creative world for designing a build away from your home. Choose **Structure workshop** on the main menu. It is always creative, at midday, with no animals. Your current world is saved first.

Build as you would anywhere, then save the build as a blueprint. Choose **Leave workshop** to return to the world you came from. The flat ground is never part of a blueprint, and you can travel without reaching an edge.
The flat workshop has not been checked in play yet. This page follows the game source and its tests.

Workshops made before this change are listed in **Worlds** with **(legacy workshop)**. Opening one keeps its original terrain, platform, player position and builds. The main menu makes a new flat workshop and does not change the old save.
Move a build from a legacy workshop

items: Open the legacy workshop from **Worlds**.
Save the build as a blueprint (see Save a blueprint, creative above).
Choose **Leave workshop** to return to your world, then choose **Structure workshop** on the main menu.
Select the saved blueprint and check its ghost in the new workshop.
Keep the legacy workshop until you have checked the copy. It stays available for more edits.

blocks.text: Sharing or importing blueprints is not in this version. Saving a blueprint in survival is not checked in play yet. They are tracked in the {{structure-workshop-blueprints|feature ledger}}.
Press [[O]] to open the library. Each saved structure has its own picture. The picked one is shown large, with its size and piece count.

rows: Pick the previous or next structure.
Delete the picked structure. Press it twice to confirm.

blocks.text: Rename writes the new file before the old one is removed, so a failed rename keeps the original. The library holds up to 64 structures. Click the search field above the list and type part of a name to narrow it. Enter ends the search and keeps the matches, and Up and Down pick among them.
Checked at Voxelgame 9f915bcb. Not yet play-tested for this guide.

rows: The same actions, in the E > Build tab (Creative).

blocks.text: In Creative, undo covers brush actions, blueprints, single blocks placed and blocks or trees you mined. Door moves, chest refinishing and furniture steps go into the same history, so [[Ctrl+Z]] always takes back your newest step first. The status line says what it undid, for example "Undid building" or "Undid door move". The history holds your last 32 steps at most. On a server, undoing a door move, chest refinishing or furniture step waits for the server to confirm. {{build-undo-redo}}

Undo is refused with "Undo blocked" if the cells changed since or if it would put a block inside you. At the save's edit limit it says "Save edit budget reached". It also stops, and says why, where a chest, door, furniture or the Home crate is in the way. Survival block edits and explosions are not recorded, but in Survival [[Ctrl+Z]] still undoes furniture steps and chest refinishing; see {{guide:furniture-and-carpentry|Furniture and carpentry}}. History is cleared when you leave the world.

In creative, E > Build has the searchable catalog. Choose **+ Tools** to open the brush controls, Undo and Redo, four preset palettes and Save palette. Survival gains a restricted carpentry Build tab while a Furniture hammer is in your pack. {{creative-catalog}} {{build-workspace-palettes}}

items: Click an ordinary catalog item to take one. Shift-click to take as many as fit in your pack. Furniture plans select a reusable construction choice instead of adding a carried item.
Right-click an item to remove one you carry. Shift-right-click removes all of them.
Middle-click an item to star it.
Hover an item and press 1 to 0, or drag it onto a slot, to bind it to the hotbar.
In creative, open **+ Tools**, then click Timber, Masonry, Coastal or Garden to fill the ten quick slots with that set. Slot 1 is selected.
Click Save palette to store your current ten slots.
Shift-click Save palette to load them back.

blocks.text: A preset replaces all ten quick slots. Click Save palette first if you want to keep them.

guides.title: Sailing a boat
guides.headline:
Launch it, steer it,
read the wind.
guides.summary: Launch and pack up the Small sailing boat, take the helm, set the sails, tack upwind and save your boats.
guides.lead: The Small sailing boat floats on any water in the game. You launch it from the hotbar, steer it from the helm and set the sails to catch the wind. Boats are not available on multiplayer servers yet.

verification.method: Launch, pack, helm keys, sail and steering behaviour, wind speeds and saving come from the feature ledger, which cites the game source lines for each entry. The 6 m launch and pack range, 9 m helm range, 18 capacity of free pack room, 8-boat limit and 45 degree no-push zone are code values.
verification.limits: Source-checked, not play-tested in this guide and without screenshots. Test the tacking advice and the 45 degree no-push zone on open water before you rely on them.

blocks.text: Crafting the Small sailing boat selects it, ready to launch. Launching it works in creative and survival, and the boat can float on any water: sea, lakes and all six water types, at their real surface height. {{sailing-launch-and-pack}}

items: Select the Small sailing boat in your hotbar or inventory.
Look at open water within 6 m and right-click. The boat appears on the water.
In survival, the launch uses one boat item. In creative, the boat comes from the catalog and no item is used.

blocks.text: The launch needs water under the whole hull and clear room for the mast. If it fails, the game says "Boat needs clear water and room for its hull and mast (8 boats maximum)" and nothing is used. You can have up to 8 boats in the world at once.
Packing a boat puts it back into your pack, so you can carry it to another lake or sea. {{sailing-launch-and-pack}}

items: Walk up to a boat that has nobody at the helm and look at it from within 6 m.
Hold Shift and right-click. You can hold any item.
The boat goes into your pack. In survival, the boat item comes back to you.
You need 18 capacity of free pack room. A boat that is too heavy for your pack cannot be packed.
A boat with 0 health (wrecked) cannot be boarded or packed. The game clears it the next time you launch a boat.

blocks.text: Boats are not available on multiplayer servers yet. The game refuses with "Boats aren't available on servers yet".
You can walk and jump on the wooden deck like normal ground. The helm is where you steer and set the sails. {{sailing-helm-controls}}

rows: Take the helm, or step back to the cockpit. You must be within 9 m of the boat or on its deck.
Raise the sails. They follow over about 2 seconds.
Steer left or right. The rudder eases in and recentres.
Switch between first-person and chase view.
Look around freely without turning the boat.

items: There is no reverse. Lower the sails to slow down, and steer to turn.
The boat can turn while it is stopped.

The boat stops dead if its hull would run aground or hit another boat. It can only turn where the new heading still has water under the whole hull. If the boat is stuck on the shore, pack it up and launch it again.
Stepping off the helm stops the boat at once. Opening your pack with E pauses it.

blocks.text: Each world has one wind direction, and it never changes. The wind strength depends on the weather: about 2.8 m/s in clear weather and up to 8.5 m/s in a thunderstorm. Seasons do not change the wind. {{sailing-wind-and-tacking}}

items: Running with the wind (sailing straight downwind) is fastest.
Sailing across the wind gives about two-thirds of the wind speed.
Within 45 degrees of sailing straight into the wind, the sails give no push. To go upwind, zig-zag: sail one side of the wind, then turn across it to the other side. This is called tacking.

blocks.text: Read the flags

items: The red pennant at the top of the mast points downwind, the way the air travels.
The HUD flag shows the wind with the bow of your boat at the top of the screen.

blocks.text: The HUD bearing reads "TO n DEG", but it is not a compass bearing. 0 degrees points to +Z, which is south on the map, and 90 degrees points to +X, which is east. Use the flags to judge the wind.
Up to 8 launched boats are saved with their position, heading and health. Your boats are still there when you load the world. {{sailing-saving}}
If you save while at the helm, you reload standing in the stopped boat's cockpit, not at the helm. Press V to take the helm again.

guides.title: Settings and performance
guides.headline:
Settings,
and how to make the game run smoothly.
guides.summary: Find graphics, audio, controls and interface preferences, change keys and reduce rendering work.
guides.lead: In a world, press Esc and choose Settings; on the start menu, choose Settings directly. Most preferences follow you between worlds.

verification.method: Every Settings group, page, option name, range, default and help text, the graphics presets, search and reset, key capture, the F3/F7/F8/F9 overlays, audio mixing, nature-ambience rules and the shared preference file were re-checked against Voxelgame 251b9e46aeefd207a5e34046dd8a973c2a2cb480 source on 2026-11-08. Normal-window GPU timing remains separate from offscreen developer profiling.
verification.limits: Source-checked at Voxelgame 251b9e46 on 8 November 2026; not play-tested. No FPS or GPU-memory benchmark, desktop idle test or new screenshot was made. Old hardware figures are not presented as current results.

items: In a world, press Esc and choose Settings. On the start menu, choose Settings directly. Ctrl+F on the pause menu opens Settings with search ready.
Choose Graphics, Audio, Controls, Gameplay, Interface or Advanced, then a subpage.

Click Find settings or press Ctrl+F, then type. A setting matches when every word appears in its group, page, name or help. Enter or Tab leaves the field; Up/Down then steps through matches on every page. Ctrl+Backspace clears the search.

rows: Previous / next subpage; on Key bindings, previous / next page of actions.
Select a row or search result.
Step the selected value back / forward.
Click a chip or < >, drag a slider
Restore this page’s defaults, outside text entry. On Key bindings, Backspace or Reset keys restores every key.

blocks.text: Changes apply immediately. Hover a label for help. Back or Esc returns to the pause menu or start menu; Resume returns to play. Local play pauses; connected servers continue. {{settings-menu}}

items: **Graphics > Display** holds Graphics preset, Field of view, Horizon distance, Atmospheric fog, Frame limit, Shader and Chunk fade-in.

**Graphics preset** sets five of them at once. Low: Shader None, 32 chunks, Dense fog, no fade-in, 60 FPS. Balanced (the defaults): Fast, 64 chunks, Balanced fog, fade-in, 60 FPS. High: Fast, 128 chunks, Balanced fog, fade-in, 120 FPS. Cinematic: Cinematic, 192 chunks, Light fog, fade-in, 60 FPS. Editing one of those five shows Custom; Field of view is not part of a preset.

**Shader** offers None, Fast (default) or Cinematic. None is plain voxel lighting; Fast adds sun shadows, sun rays and haze; Cinematic refines shadows and rays and adds reflective water, at extra frame time. {{shader-tiers}}

**Horizon distance** offers 8, 16, 32, 48, 64 (default), 96, 128, 192, 256, 512 and 1024 chunks. One chunk is 16 m; the largest radius is about 16 km. It sets only the low-detail distant view; full-detail terrain near you stays at nine chunks. {{horizon-distance}}
**Frame limit** is 60 (default), 120, 240 or Unlimited. A cap is not a guaranteed frame rate. There is no separate vsync setting; Frame limit paces the frames. {{frame-limit}}

**Atmospheric fog** is Light, Balanced (default) or Dense; haze strength follows Horizon distance. **Field of view** is 60–96° in 2° steps (default 72°). **Chunk fade-in** (on by default) fades newly loaded terrain in over 0.6 seconds. {{atmospheric-fog}} {{field-of-view}} {{chunk-fade-in}}
**Controls > Mouse** has separate Horizontal and Vertical sensitivity (50–200% in 10% steps, default 100%) and Invert mouse Y.

**Controls > Key bindings** changes gameplay keys. Select an action and press Enter (or click it), then press the new key. Esc cancels and Delete leaves the action unbound. Esc, F6, F11 and Print Screen cannot be assigned. A key used by two actions shows “Conflict: …”. Defaults are in {{guide:controls-reference|Controls reference}}.
**Gameplay > Movement** has Camera bob, Speed FOV, Damage bob (Off, Reduced or Full) and Hold/Toggle for Sprint, Sneak and Crawl. Sprint and Sneak default to Hold; Crawl defaults to Toggle.

**Interface > Layout** has GUI size (Auto, Small, Normal or Large), UI scale (75–200% in 5% steps), HUD text only, Target info (F2), HUD compass and Compact map heading. Scale is capped so the menu fits. {{gui-size}}
**Interface > Crosshair** sets style (Cross, Dot or Brackets), size (50–200%), colour (Adaptive, White, Lime or Cyan) and opacity (25–100%). Every style keeps accuracy feedback.

**Interface > Accessibility** has Color vision palettes for information overlays, High contrast, Reduce motion, Low survival warning and Warning pulse. The warning appears when health, food, water or stamina falls to 10, 20, 30 or 40% (default 20%). Reduce motion turns off camera bob, FOV kick, blast shake, fades and pulses; static warnings remain.

**Audio > Volume** has Master, Music, Effects, Ambience and UI volume, each 0–100% (default 100%). Arrow keys move them 5% at a time. Master scales every category; zero on one category mutes only that category. {{master-volume}}

**Audio > Music** turns music on or off, sets Music speed from 0.5× to 2.0× in 0.1× steps (tempo and pitch; effects keep their speed) and picks the Previous or Next song. Below it you see the current title, “No music installed”, or a sound problem: “Sound unavailable: install alsa-utils” on Linux, or “install ffplay (FFmpeg)” on Windows and macOS. {{music-player}}

blocks.text: Set Ambience volume to zero to silence nature sounds while keeping effects and music. Nature sounds continue behind in-world menus but stop underwater and on the start menu. {{nature-ambience}}

**Advanced > Diagnostics** has LOD view, Voxel view, Distant terrain, Performance, Chunk borders and FPS and coordinates; Mesh view is shown as unavailable. The FPS box is on by default and shows measured FPS with the limit (or UNCAPPED), your X, Y and Z position and the biome. It hides while a menu is open. {{fps-coordinates-readout}}

rows: Show or hide the performance overlay: CPU work over the last half second, frame time against the frame budget, the worst recent frame and a spike count. The budget follows Frame limit (Unlimited uses 60 FPS); a spike is a frame over twice the budget and at least 25 ms.
Show or hide 16 m chunk borders. Your current chunk is gold; neighbours are cyan.
Cycle the LOD view: Off, Tint and Colors. With the standard palette, cyan is full detail; green, blue, yellow, orange, purple and red mark the 0.5 to 16 m distant stages.
Turn all three overlays off if any is on; otherwise turn all on, with LOD view in Tint.

blocks.text: The keys above are defaults and can be reassigned. Performance, Chunk borders and LOD view are not saved: after a restart they are off, and the FPS box is on again. {{diagnostic-overlays}} {{performance-overlay}}

items: **Voxel view**: Off (default), Edges, which tints every block border, or X-ray, which draws only the outlines. {{voxel-view}}

**Distant terrain**: on by default. It draws the low-detail horizon beyond the nearby chunks. Turning it off saves work on slow machines. The view then ends at the nearby loaded terrain, where new chunks appear as you move. {{distant-terrain-toggle}}
Try Graphics > Display > Graphics preset > Low: plain shading, 32-chunk horizon, dense fog, no terrain fade and a 60 FPS limit.
If needed, lower Horizon distance to 16 or 8 chunks, or turn Advanced > Diagnostics > Distant terrain off. The distant view becomes shorter.
Use the default F3 key to compare frame time with the frame budget. Compare the same place and settings before drawing conclusions.

blocks.text: The normal window does not provide live GPU pass timings. This guide has no current hardware benchmark or promised frame-rate gain. {{performance-overlay}}

Graphics, audio, interface preferences and key bindings follow the player between worlds. They save automatically about half a second after a change and when you quit; on Linux the file is ~/.config/voxelgame/settings. If it cannot be read, the game leaves it untouched, stops saving preferences and shows “Settings not saved …”; fix the file and restart. Time, weather and season belong to each world, under Gameplay > World; they are read-only in survival. For profile locations and recovery, see {{guide:install-and-worlds|Install, update and find your worlds}}. {{per-world-settings}}
The 1024-chunk horizon is available as an optional distant view. No current hardware performance result is supplied here. {{horizon-1024}}
Live GPU pass timings in ordinary play remain planned. The normal window’s GPU box reports unavailable. {{gpu-timing-live}}

The native app requests that the desktop stay awake while its window is focused and visible, including menus. Desktop support varies; it releases the request on focus loss or hiding. {{display-awake}}

guides.title: Explosives: TNT and dynamite
guides.headline:
Blow up blocks
with TNT and dynamite.
guides.summary: Place and light TNT with G, read the blast reach, throw dynamite, and see which explosives survival can craft.
guides.lead: TNT and dynamite break blocks in a wide circle. Blasted blocks are destroyed, not collected. Creative players can use them freely. In survival, both need Glow crystal, which the world does not generate naturally.

verification.method: Controls, fuse times, blast reach, damage rules and dynamite throwing come from the game source at the ledger's audited commit dd29d91 (game.rs, explosives.rs, projectile.rs, ranged_input.rs, inventory.rs). Blast distances are calculated from code constants, not measured in play. On 8 November 2026 the place-and-light, dynamite and saves sections were re-checked for multiplayer servers at Voxelgame dfeb362ddeca56ff5de77fa26ccdb6e37d05192c: game.rs:2808-2820, game/net_client/tnt.rs:41-155, game/ranged_input.rs:76-97, game/net_client/dynamite_throws.rs:61-212, session/tnt.rs:40-137, session/tnt/dynamite.rs:17-110 and docs/MULTIPLAYER.md:2500-2539. The other sections keep the dd29d91 receipt.
verification.limits: Source-checked, not play-tested in this guide. The server behaviour was source-checked at Voxelgame dfeb362d on 8 November 2026; no server session was run. No explosion screenshots exist yet, so the blast sizes are not checked against a headless capture.

items: Select TNT in your hotbar.
Right click a surface to place a whole block. Hold Shift and right click to place one half-metre charge.
Aim at the TNT, within 6 m, and press [[G]].
Step back. The fuse lasts 2.6 seconds.

rows: Light the aimed TNT and every TNT piece touching it, even diagonally.
Mine TNT back without lighting it.

blocks.text: Lit TNT pops loose and can fall, roll or float before it blows. Touching pieces go off together as one blast. {{tnt-place-and-ignite}}

On a multiplayer server, [[G]] asks the server to light the TNT. The status line says "Requesting TNT ignition | move away"; wait for the reply before you use another explosive. The server checks that you can reach the TNT and are allowed to build there. It then says, for example, "8-charge TNT cluster ignited by server | move away". A refusal starts with "TNT ignition refused:" and gives the reason. If the server restarts while a fuse burns, that TNT is lost.

items: One half-metre charge or one dynamite stick: about 1.5 m.
One whole TNT block: about 4.25 m.
A touching group of TNT: up to about 10.5 m, which needs about 62 touching TNT blocks.

blocks.text: A whole TNT block cannot break obsidian. Solid stone only gives way close to the charge. Blocks between the charge and a target absorb part of the blast, and water absorbs a lot of it. {{explosion-effects}}
Explosions cannot be undone. Blasted blocks are gone. The status line counts cleared half-metre voxels.
In survival, players near a blast lose health and are knocked back. Creative players take no damage. Creatures are hurt in both modes.
Stand well back before you light a group. The blast reaches about 10.5 m from the largest group.

items: Select Dynamite in your hotbar.
Hold right click to wind up. A longer wind-up throws farther.
Release to throw. The fuse starts on release.
Take cover. The stick goes off 2.3 seconds after you throw it, where it is then. It sticks to the first surface it hits.

rows: Wind up and throw a dynamite stick.

items: The stick sticks to the first surface it hits, including walls and ceilings.
You cannot place blocks while you hold dynamite.
Opening a menu cancels a wind-up.
Creative throws are unlimited. Survival uses one stick per throw. A throw that cannot fly keeps the stick.

On a multiplayer server, releasing asks the server to throw. The status line says "Requesting dynamite throw", then "Dynamite thrown by server". Wait for the reply before you throw again. A refused throw keeps the stick, for example "Wait for the server to finish the current action | dynamite kept". In Survival the server spends one stick when it accepts the throw; Creative throws stay free.

blocks.text: {{dynamite-throwing}}

sections.title: Crafting TNT and dynamite in survival

blocks.text: Both recipes need Glow crystal. The world does not generate it naturally, and a survival world usually has one half-metre piece at the Stone overlook landmark. The game places that landmark only when it finds a dry flat spot near its fixed base. You cannot make TNT or dynamite from gathered materials alone. {{lumen-crystal-supply}}
One TNT recipe makes 8 pieces, one whole block. Two dynamite sticks need 4 TNT and 2 Paper screens.

sections.title: What a quit or reload does

items: Lit TNT and burning dynamite are not saved. Quitting during a fuse loses that TNT.
On a multiplayer server, lit TNT and burning dynamite are lost if the server restarts. Blasted ground, injuries and loot are kept.
Explosions are not recorded in build history.

guides.title: Day, night and weather
guides.headline:
Day, night and weather
what changes and when.
guides.summary: A day lasts 20 minutes. Weather follows a 30-minute pattern in every world, rain stops at roofs, and creative players can hold the time and weather.
guides.lead: A full day and night lasts 20 real minutes. Weather in a world follows the same 30-minute pattern, so you can plan around rain and storms. Nothing skips the night: the sun keeps moving, and you cannot sleep through it.

verification.method: Re-checked against the game source at Voxelgame 251b9e46 on 8 November 2026: day length, start time and sun path (environment.rs, game.rs, frame.rs), the night sky (shader.wgsl), farm animals resting at night (entities), beds and Home rest leaving the clock alone (furniture/resting.rs, home.rs), the weather order, step length and blending, the rain, cloud, fog and wind of each weather, lightning and thunder timing (environment.rs), rain stopping at blocks and at the cloud ceiling (precipitation.rs), roof rain and wildlife sounds (ambience.rs), sailing wind (sailing.rs), the clock pausing in menus (game.rs), the shared server clock (session.rs, server host, net bridge) and the Gameplay > World rows (settings.rs, ui.rs, music_settings.rs, settings_search.rs). The cloud heights still match the native before/after captures and automated altitude tests recorded at Voxelgame 61a4257 on 15 October 2026; those captures were not repeated.
verification.limits: Source-checked at Voxelgame 251b9e46 on 8 November 2026; not play-tested. No new captures were taken. No public weather or night photographs have been added.

blocks.text: One day and night lasts 20 real minutes. The sun is up for about 10 minutes and down for about 10. New worlds start about a minute after sunrise. {{day-night-cycle}}

items: Night is darker and the moon is out. On clear nights you also see stars and the Milky Way; cloud hides them. Nothing dangerous happens at night because of the time of day.
Cows, sheep, pigs and chickens stop wandering and rest on dry ground from about a minute after sunset until about a minute before sunrise. An animal you hit still runs.

You cannot sleep or skip the night. Lying in a bed does not pass time ({{guide:storage-beds-and-lamps|Storage, beds and lamps}}), and **Rest / set respawn** at your Home crate only sets your respawn point and refills stamina.

Birds sing near trees from sunrise until about midday. Night wildlife sounds take over after dark. Both are quieter in rain and silent under a roof, high above the ground, on coasts and in deserts, snowy or volcanic land.
In a single-player world, time stops while the pause menu, Settings or the fullscreen map is open. On a server the clock keeps running.

blocks.text: Day and night do not cause ambient-temperature survival penalties. {{temperature-shelter}}

items: The weather cycle takes 30 minutes. Each step lasts 3 minutes.
The order is clear, cloudy, rain, cloudy, partly cloudy, foggy, cloudy, rainstorm, thunderstorm, cloudy. Then it starts again.
Rain, cloud, mist and wind blend over about 15 seconds when the step changes, so there is no sudden switch.

blocks.text: Each world starts at a different point in the cycle. The whole world shares one weather pattern, so rain falls over deserts too. There is no snowfall. To see the current step, press [[Esc]], choose **Settings** and open **Gameplay > World**: the Weather row reads, for example, **Auto / rain**. {{automatic-weather}}

items: **Clear**: a cloudless sky. **Partly cloudy**: scattered clouds. **Cloudy**: grey overcast. None of them rain.
**Rain**: steady rain and a light breeze.
**Rainstorm**: heavy rain and strong wind, with no lightning.
**Thunderstorm**: the heaviest rain, the strongest wind, and lightning with thunder.
**Foggy**: thick mist that cuts visibility, with no rain.
Rain stops at the first solid or liquid block, so a roof you build keeps the rain off you.
Under a roof, rain is heard as a softer patter on the roof.
Overcast and rain darken the sky, and rain thickens the haze.
In a thunderstorm, lightning lights up the sky and land about every 18 seconds, and thunder follows one to three seconds later. Lightning does not damage you or set anything on fire.
Cloud banks begin at 1,200, 1,800 and 2,500 metres above world zero.
Rain and its sound fade as you climb through the lowest cloud bank and stop by 1,600 metres. Flying above the clouds does not stop rain in the world below.
Weather never hurts you. Rain, storms and fog have no health, food, water or temperature penalty.
The music leans towards songs that suit the time of day, rain, storms and fog.

blocks.text: Wind strength changes with the weather, from about 2.8 m/s in clear weather to 8.5 m/s in a thunderstorm, so sailing is affected too. {{sailing-wind-and-tacking}}

sections.title: Hold the time or weather in creative

items: Press [[Esc]], choose **Settings**, then open **Gameplay > World**.
On the **Time of day** row, click **<** or **>** to step through Cycle, Dawn, Day, Dusk and Night. Cycle goes back to the normal day.
On the **Weather** row, step through Auto, Clear, Partly cloudy, Cloudy, Rain, Rainstorm, Thunderstorm and Foggy. Auto goes back to the normal pattern.

rows: Hold the sun at sunrise, midday or sunset, or hold the moon at midnight.
Dry skies with no cloud, scattered cloud or overcast.
Steady rain, or heavy rain without lightning.
Heavy rain with lightning and thunder.

blocks.text: You can also pick a row with the Up / Down arrow keys and change it with Left / Right or [[Enter]]; right-click a row to step it back. Both lists wrap round. **Reset page** sets Time of day back to Cycle and Weather and Season back to Auto.

A held time or weather is saved with the world and stays in force if you switch to survival with [[F4]]. In survival the rows only show the current state; trying to change one says **Time, weather, and season controls are read-only in survival**. {{creative-world-controls}}
On a server, everyone shares the server's time, weather and season. Changes in this tab do not reach the server and are replaced within a few seconds.

sections.title: Planned, not in the game yet

blocks.text: Planned: darker nights, and regional weather where different parts of a world get different weather. Until these ship, the day length and weather pattern above are the same everywhere.

guides.title: Saves and world files
guides.headline:
Saves and world files
what is kept, and the limits.
guides.summary: Save, back up and recover a world. Find what persists and how the 200,000-block and 8 MiB limits apply.
guides.lead: Your world file keeps your character, carried items and changes to the world. Untouched terrain is rebuilt from the saved seed and generation. Display, audio and input preferences are shared across worlds.

verification.method: What a save keeps comes from the save writer's section list (crates/voxelgame-core/src/save/write.rs) and the session-only settings in the ledger. Limits and messages were checked against Voxelgame 51169272: 8 MiB and 200,000-edit constants and the 190,000 warning threshold (save.rs, game.rs), the 'saves' refusals and the version checks (save.rs, load.rs). Opening rules come from src/app.rs and src/single_instance.rs. Targeted compatibility clarification at 35cfc2f8: the serialized temperature field remains inert in survival.rs; other save evidence retains its original audit. Targeted 5 November source follow-up at aa136e0103ce5599c6d8a9f70c669dbc758b7357: current save sections, shared preferences, generation 12, Worlds backup/recovery and stopped-host retry/choice paths. Existing unrelated opening-screen evidence keeps its earlier receipt. The game’s dated WORLD_BACKUP_20261016 verification records offscreen backup recovery; this wiki pass did not rerun it. Targeted 8 November 2026 source follow-up at Voxelgame dfeb362ddeca56ff5de77fa26ccdb6e37d05192c: F6 confirms only after a local write (src/app.rs), the 8 MiB refusal in the save encoder and writer (save.rs), size refusals on servers (session/crafting.rs, creatures.rs, items.rs, water.rs and home/*.rs), dedicated-server save waits (voxelgame-server host/furniture/durability/stock.rs), the seat and bed exit check before saving (save/write.rs, game/furniture/resting.rs, seating.rs) and saved lamp and stove state (furniture/lamp_state.rs, furniture/cooking.rs).
verification.limits: Source-checked in this follow-up; no new game process, native save/fault injection, LAN play or screenshot capture. Existing loading-screen prose retains its earlier audit. Backup and stopped-host instructions need integration browser review; an uncheckpointed session is not guaranteed to survive a restart. The 8 November follow-up was source-checked at Voxelgame dfeb362d on 8 November 2026; not play-tested, with no game process, server or save-fault run.

blocks.text: Saving writes the whole world file. It keeps:

items: Your position, view direction and game mode (creative or survival).
In survival: health, hunger, thirst and stamina. A legacy temperature value is retained for compatibility and has no gameplay effect.
Your inventory, hotbar bindings and selected slot, and the tool you hold.
Every block you changed, including water and door state.
Time of day, weather and season controls.
Your home crate and rest point, chest contents and one saved build palette.
Placed furniture with its stored items, whether each lamp is switched on, and a stove's contents and unfinished batch.
Journal places, expedition finds, milestones and the map destination.
Up to 8 sailing boats.
Player-hatched animals and dropped item stacks. {{save-contents}}

blocks.text: Procedural wildlife, flying projectiles and primed TNT are not saved. Temporary diagnostic overlays also reset. Display, audio and input preferences are shared separately; a world file still contains older settings fields for compatibility.

items: [[F6]] saves now. “World saved safely” appears only after the world file is written, including the world you host. In a world you joined, or a session started with --no-save, F6 writes nothing and says “This session does not save the world locally”.
Autosave checks about every 30 seconds and saves when world state has changed.
Choosing Main menu, Save & quit or Quit, pressing [[Ctrl]]+[[Q]], closing the window, or loading or creating another world saves first.
Main menu keeps a hosted world running. Use **Stop hosting** on the Multiplayer page to end hosting.

blocks.text: A failed save shows “Save refused:” with the reason and keeps a visible warning until a save succeeds. If saving fails while you are quitting, the game stays open so you can fix the problem and retry. {{saving}}

If you save while sitting or lying in a bed, the world reopens with you standing beside it. Saving needs a clear spot to stand there; otherwise it is refused with 'Bed exit blocked; cannot save an embedded player' or 'Seat exit blocked; cannot save an embedded player'. Make room and save again.
In a world you joined, the server keeps the world. A dedicated server confirms most actions only after it has saved them; see {{guide:not-in-the-game-yet|Multiplayer and feature limits}}.
If a stopped host cannot recover your pack

items: Keep the session open. If the save before stopping failed, the world is still hosted; fix the reported problem and try **Stop hosting** again.
If hosting has stopped and pack recovery is blocked, press [[F6]] to retry. **Continue** returns to the repair session so you can adjust conflicting Creative catalogue choices.

Press [[Shift]]+[[F6]] to inspect the recovery choice. You can keep current choices, or hold the offered recovery action for 3 seconds. **Use final pack** selects the host’s final pack and mode, setting aside conflicting catalogue changes. If the final world or pack is unavailable, **Use last saved world** restores the saved world and its matching pack together.
The explicit choice first preserves an independent recovery copy. If writing that copy or a checkpoint fails, keep the session open and follow the reported error before retrying.

blocks.text: An unresolved pack blocks ordinary saving, world replacement and quitting. Recovery files protect a successfully recorded checkpoint; do not remove them to bypass the choice. The dialog explains which later state will be set aside. {{mp-menu-lan-hosting}}

items: Each world file is capped at 8 MiB. A save that would be bigger is refused with “Save refused: refusing to exceed the 8 MiB debug-save safety budget”, and the existing file stays as it was.
A world holds up to 200,000 changed blocks. Beyond that, new building is refused with 'Save edit budget reached'. Spreading water never pushes a save past the limit.
From 190,000 changed blocks, the status line warns 'saving stops at 200000' about every 20 seconds.
A home crate, blueprint or structure that would go past the limit is not placed.

On a hosted or dedicated server, the size cap also limits other actions, such as crafting, hitting animals, moving or dropping items and filling flasks. If the world file would go over, the server refuses with a message ending 'would exceed the save budget or saved state is invalid', for example 'Crafting would exceed the save budget or saved state is invalid'. An exact fit is allowed, and actions that make the save smaller still work.

blocks.text: Make and reopen a backup

items: Open **Worlds**, select a saved world and choose **Create backup** or press [[Ctrl]]+[[B]]. Stop hosting first if this is the hosted world.
Wait for **Backup ready** and keep the location shown. A completed backup ends in backups/backup-<time>-<process>-<sequence>/snapshot/. The active local world is saved before copying.
To reopen a backup, close the game and copy the whole completed **snapshot** folder into a new folder such as worlds/recovered-house/. Keep the original world and the backup.
Start the game and open the new copy from **Worlds**. A .pending folder is an unfinished attempt, not a completed backup.

blocks.text: Backups contain the save and its available name, preview and session-history files. They are stored beside worlds, so deleting the source world does not delete the backup. Finish any outstanding save recovery before making an ordinary backup or duplicate. {{world-backups}} {{save-limits}}

items: A world keeps the terrain generation it was created with. Create world defaults to generation 12 and also offers older generations; loading or updating a world preserves its saved choice. {{world-generation-version}}
A world saved before the half-metre block grid is refused with 'world predates the half-metre voxel grid; a new world is required'. Create a new world instead.
A world saved by a newer version of the game is refused by an older one with 'world was saved by a newer version of voxelgame'. Update the game to open it.
A file that is not a Voxelgame save is refused with 'not a voxelgame save'.

blocks.text: If a world will not open, read {{unreadable-save}}. {{save-compatibility}}

items: Only one copy of the game runs per user. Opening it again brings the open window to the front and shows 'Voxelgame was already open; click the world to recapture the mouse'. {{single-instance}}

When the game first opens, a tumbling wireframe cube settles into the Voxelgame logo above the current loading stage and an activity bar. Later world loads show only the stage and the bar. There is no percentage. {{loading-screen}}

guides.title: Animal spawning, calls and spawn eggs
guides.headline:
Animal spawning, calls and spawn eggs
where animals appear, and how to place them.
guides.summary: Wild animals appear around you as you explore, depending on the biome. Up to 36 can be around you at once. Creative mode has a spawn egg for each of the 94 species.
guides.lead: Wild animals appear on their own as you walk, sail and fly around the world. Which ones you see depends on the biome and nearby water. This page covers where animals appear, how many there can be, which species call, and how to use creative spawn eggs.

verification.method: Re-checked on 8 November 2026 at Voxelgame 251b9e46aeefd207a5e34046dd8a973c2a2cb480. Spawning: crates/voxelgame-core/src/entities/mod.rs (36-animal cap at line 100; per-species caps at 677-710; the 25 squares of 32 m, the one-in-five empty squares, the 96 m height check, the water-depth rule and natural ground at 1696-1909; square memory at 1924-1955; 180 m removal at 1412-1420), entities/biome_species.rs:10-327 (biome species groups, swans, empty volcanic biomes), entities/ambient_spawn.rs:7-29 (natural ground) and session.rs:735-747 (one shared population on a server). Swimming: entities/aquatic_cruise.rs:164-278 and 324-367, and entities/mod.rs:1157-1167 (fish that keep their distance). Calls: entities/mod.rs:456-485 and 999-1040, game/audio.rs:154-170, events.rs:74-86 and 155-160, ambience.rs:190-209, entities/idle_behaviour.rs:15-19 and src/audio.rs:889-917. Species: Species::ALL (94 entries) and name() in entities/mod.rs:359-584. Eggs: ui.rs:249 and 276-277, game/hotbar.rs:217-228, game/ranged_input.rs:51-163, projectile.rs:1476-1526, entities/hatching.rs:72-132, entities/persistence.rs:117-194, game.rs:2203-2212, session/eggs.rs:92-150 and game/net_client/egg_throws.rs:62-97 and 178-194. A search of the game code found no spawn-egg crafting recipe.
verification.limits: Source-checked at Voxelgame 251b9e46 on 8 November 2026; not play-tested. No captures of spawned animals exist yet. Exact spawn counts depend on the terrain around you, so the numbers here are caps, not what you will always see.

blocks.text: As you move, the game checks the 25 squares of ground around you, each about 32 m across. About one square in five is left empty. In the others, one animal may appear, picked from the species that fit that biome. In a given world, a square always offers the same species at the same spot. {{animal-natural-spawning}}

items: Up to 36 wild animals can be around you at the same time. On a server, all players share the same animals and the same limit.
Each biome has its own small group of species. A meadow, a forest and a snowy tundra have different animals.
Wetland fens, flooded grasslands, inland deltas and river deltas can have swans.
Volcanic fields, meteor fields, geyser basins and surface lava tubes have no wild animals.

Each species has a cap. Whales, orcas and giant squid: 1 at a time. Wolves, bears, foxes, crocodiles, lions, tigers and panthers: 3. Boars, goats, buffalo, bison and giraffes: 5. Rabbits, frogs, ducks, salmon, trout and carp: 8. Tiny animals such as butterflies, flies and ants: 10. Most others: 4 to 7.
Fish and other swimmers appear only where the water is deep enough below sea level for their body.
Land animals appear only on natural ground such as grass, dirt, sand, snow, ice or stone. They never appear on planks, bricks, plaster, marble, glass or roof tiles.

blocks.text: New animals do not appear while you are more than 96 m above or below the ground. Over water, the sea surface counts as the ground. Spawning starts again once you are back within 96 m.

Any wild animal more than 180 m from you is removed from the world. Each square gets one try while you stay nearby. It is tried again only after you have moved roughly 250 m away and come back, so animals you hunt are not replaced straight away. Wild animals are not saved: after you load a world, they appear afresh.
Animals you hatched from eggs are set aside instead. They are saved with the world and come back when you return within 180 m. {{animal-spawn-eggs}}
Fish and other water animals do not walk and stand like land animals. Each species follows one of three swimming styles.

items: Whales, orcas, hammerhead and frilled sharks, and flying fish keep travelling in open water. Now and then they glide, slowing to about half speed.
Salmon, trout, carp, catfish, Devil's Hole pupfish and triops swim in short bouts and hold still between them.
Blobfish, comb jellies and giant squid mostly hover or drift slowly.
A swimmer turns away from shores, walls and the edge of loaded terrain before it reaches them. If it has no open route, it holds still.
A hurt swimmer flees at full speed. Salmon, trout and carp also dart away when you come within about 5 m.

blocks.text: You cannot steer wild animals. Their swimming is set by the game and is source-checked, not play-tested in this guide.

25 species make calls: cows, pigs, chickens, sheep, goats, frogs, gulls, geese, swans, ducks, wild horses, wolves, crows, bears, boars, buffalo, bison, elephants, turkeys, blue jays, foxes, lions, tigers, snow leopards and panthers. {{animal-calls}}

items: You hear a call from an animal within about 24 m. The closer it is, the louder and clearer it sounds.
At most one call plays every 7 to 13 seconds. When several animals are close, the game picks one caller at a time and rotates through them.
A call follows the animal while it plays. You hear it from the animal's side, and it gets louder or quieter as you or the animal move.
Blue jays and crows call only while morning birdsong plays: between sunrise and noon, near trees, outdoors and not in heavy rain.
Cows, sheep, pigs and chickens rest at night and stay quiet while they rest.

blocks.text: The game has 94 animal species, from cows and rabbits to whales, giant squid, bats and swans. Each one has its own spawn cap and biome groups. {{animal-species-roster}}

Cow, pig, chicken, deer, sheep, rabbit, fox, boar, goat, frog, gull, goose, buffalo, duck, beaver, wild horse, bear, zebra, giraffe, elephant, hippo, salmon, trout, carp, turkey, peafowl, wolf, panther, tiger, lion, crab, turtle, crocodile, whale, ostrich, kangaroo, butterfly, roadrunner, gazelle, fly, hummingbird, orca, sunbird, gorilla, rattlesnake, hammerhead shark, lobster, Komodo dragon, capuchin monkey, cave centipede, moose, raccoon, blobfish, seal, cockroach, shoebill, snow leopard, crow, alligator snapping turtle, mantis shrimp, emu, platypus, Tasmanian devil, leafcutter ant, bald eagle, tarantula hawk, frilled shark, mimic octopus, toucan, maned wolf, anaconda, anteater, gelada monkey, jerboa, terrapin, comb jelly, giant squid, Devils Hole pupfish, catfish, flying fish, potoo, mudskipper, rhinoceros, sugar glider, skunk, banana slug, blue jay, caiman, triops, bison, bat, river otter, penguin, swan.
The creative catalog has a MOBS tab with a spawn egg for each of the 94 species. The ALL tab does not list eggs. Spawn eggs cannot be crafted. {{animal-spawn-eggs}}

items: Open the creative catalog and choose the **MOBS** tab.
Take the egg of the species you want. It becomes the item you hold.
Hold the right mouse button to wind up the throw. A full wind-up takes 0.7 s and throws farther. Release it to throw the egg.
The egg flies past animals and bursts on the first block it hits. The animal hatches there.

blocks.text: A quick tap is not enough. If you release in under about 0.2 s, the game says 'Too hasty — wind up before releasing' and nothing is thrown.

items: A thrown egg can add animals above the normal 36 limit. An egg cannot hatch while 64 animals are around you, once the world keeps 64 hatched animals, or where the animal does not fit. The game then says "The egg burst, but nothing could hatch here". Eggs do hatch on built floors and roofs.
Hatched animals are saved with the world. When you move more than 180 m away they wait where they were, and they return when you come back. A hatched animal that is killed is gone for good.
In survival, a thrown egg uses one you are carrying. Eggs have no crafting recipe.

On a server, wait for the server to confirm the throw: the game says '<Animal> egg thrown by server'. If the server refuses, for example with 'Wait a moment before throwing another egg' or 'This plot belongs to another player', you keep the egg. An egg cannot hatch on another player's plot.

guides.title: Aiming, camera and on-screen feedback
guides.headline:
Aim it, read it,
feel the camera.
guides.summary: Read the crosshair and looking-at card, steady ranged aim, set the camera effects and follow the status line and collection feed.
guides.lead: This guide explains what the screen tells you while you move and aim, and the camera settings that change how movement feels.

verification.method: Crosshair spread, aim steadiness, the looking-at card, the status line, camera effects, the collection feed and water effects come from the feature ledger, which cites Voxelgame source lines. The numbers were rechecked at Voxelgame commit 0494a0ce: 6 m target reach, Speed FOV 5 degrees reaching full at 16 m/s with a 0.3 s ease, a 7 cm damage dip on hits of at least 1 HP, 5 feed rows shown for 4 s with a 0.8 s fade, and 14 splash droplets. On 8 November 2026 the looking-at section was re-checked at Voxelgame dfeb362ddeca56ff5de77fa26ccdb6e37d05192c: voxelgame-render target_ui.rs:140-147 and 260-291, hud.rs:487-492, menus_ui.rs:181-195; voxelgame-core settings.rs:65, 82-89 and 598-616.
verification.limits: Source-checked, not play-tested, and without screenshots. Judge the bob and dip strength in play. Spread amounts are internal values, so the guide describes their direction rather than exact degrees. The looking-at section was source-checked at Voxelgame dfeb362d on 8 November 2026; not play-tested.

blocks.text: The plus-shaped crosshair marks where your aim lands. It inverts the colours under it, so it stays readable over sky, grass and stone. It is hidden in the front third-person view. {{crosshair-and-reticle}}

items: With a bow, rifle or throwable in hand, the four lines spread apart as your accuracy drops. They close back into a plus as your aim steadies.
Other items keep the closed plus.

blocks.text: The spread of a bow, rifle or throwable depends on how you stand, move and shoot. {{aim-steadiness}}

rows: Widens the spread. Faster movement widens it more.
A fuller draw steadies the aim.
Raising the rifle's sights steadies the aim.

blocks.text: When you aim at a block within 6 m, a card at the top right of the screen shows it. The card sits just left of the compact map. {{looking-at-card}}

items: The card shows the block's 3D icon, name and distance. The block icon stays still, so thin blocks such as doors stay readable.
The mining advice is one of: "CREATIVE INSTANT BREAK", the recommended tool, or "NO SPECIAL TOOL NEEDED".
An animal gets its own card, with its health. Its model turns slowly.

If furniture is between you and the block, the card is hidden. The hint under the crosshair names the furniture instead, for example "TABLE | BLOCKS TERRAIN INTERACTION". You cannot mine or build through it.

rows: Hide or show the card in the world.
The same setting. It follows you between worlds.

blocks.text: The card is hidden while a menu is open.
Actions report in the status line at the top left. {{feedback-messages}}

items: Mining reports "Collected <block> x<pieces>". Pieces go straight into your pack.
A full pack says "Capacity full; block left behind". The block stays in the world.
Opening your pack says "Inventory opened".
Mined blocks throw debris and play a break sound. Dropped items are not on the ground yet.

blocks.text: A sudden loss of at least 1 HP, from a hit, a fall or a blast, plays a short hurt voice. Voices are at least half a second apart, and slow health drains stay silent. There is no red flash. The camera dip is also a cue. See the camera section below.

sections.title: Camera bob, speed view and damage dip

blocks.text: Three camera effects change how movement and hits feel. Each has a row in Settings > General. {{camera-bob-and-speed-fov}}

rows: Walking gently bobs the camera. Turn it off here.
Off or On. On widens the view by up to 5 degrees at high horizontal speed, reaching full widening at about 16 m/s. Jumps and falls do not change it.
Off, Reduced or Full. Full is the default. After a hit of at least 1 HP, the camera dips up to 7 cm at Full and half that at Reduced.

items: Speed FOV eases over about 0.3 s, so a sprint-jump does not pump the view.
Vehicles have their own speed effect, which the SPEED FOV row also turns off.
Only real health loss causes the dip. Hunger, respawn and loading do not.
The dip does not move what you aim at. Aiming and interaction still use your eye position.

blocks.text: In survival, a small feed in the lower-right corner lists what you gained, for example "+3 Oak wood". {{collection-feed}}

items: Gains come from mined blocks, felled trees, hunted animals, filled flasks, exploration finds and packed boats or homes.
A gain of an item that is already listed adds to its row.
Up to five rows show. Each stays for about 4 seconds and fades over its last 0.8 s.
Creative mining, crafting, the creative catalog, home storage and loading a save show nothing.

blocks.text: {{water-splashes}}

items: Wading into water plays a small splash. A fall at hard-landing speed plays a big splash with more droplets.
After you leave the water, walk about 2 m on dry ground before the next splash plays.
Moving through water releases bubbles and a swim sound about every 1.4 m.
Rain makes small ripple splashes on surfaces.
Boats leave no bow spray or wake.

sections.title: Held items and the character portrait

blocks.text: A block you select is shown as a small textured cube in your right hand. Tools are held on the right, and the bow sits left of centre with its own string hand. With nothing in hand, or with a block you no longer carry in survival, your bare right arm rests low on the right. Hold left click to swing a tool, bare hand or held block; bows and rifles do not swing. Placing a block plays one swing. The swing is visual only. A held sailing boat shows no hand. F1 hides held items in the clean view. {{held-items-first-person}}

Press E, stay on Pack and click Character to see a 3D portrait of your explorer. Move the pointer across it to turn the model. It shows Creative or your health, and what you are holding. There are no appearance, outfit or skin options. Remote players in multiplayer use the same fixed explorer model. {{character-tab-portrait}}

guides.title: Caves and geological landmarks
guides.headline:
Caves and geological landmarks
rare rock features, and what each one is like.
guides.summary: Some hills have a cave with one of three layouts. Rare large sites such as meteor craters, amethyst gorges and lava tubes appear on certain ground. Caves are small and bounded, not deep networks.
guides.lead: Caves and landmarks are not on every hill or valley. This page covers where caves open, the three cave layouts, and the landmark sites you can find in the base game.

verification.method: Cave rules come from crates/voxelgame-core/src/world/generator/caves.rs at Voxelgame 0494a0ce: one candidate per 384 m cell, 132 m passage radius, the 32 m hillside and 10 m entrance height rules, the 100 m entrance offset, the three layouts and the floor grade. Landmark rules come from crates/voxelgame-core/src/world/generator/regions.rs in the same commit: the 220-320 m site radius, the 512 m origin exclusion, the water and volcanic checks, the site kinds by ground type and the crater, gorge and lava tube sizes. Cave ambience comes from crates/voxelgame-core/src/ambience.rs.
verification.limits: Source-checked, not play-tested in this guide. Sizes are the code's ranges, so a site you find may look different. Sites are rare and depend on the seed, so this page does not give a map location.

blocks.text: A cave is one bounded site. Every passage stays within about 132 m of the cave's centre, so it is not a deep network of tunnels. {{caves}}
A cave needs a hill at least 32 m above sea level. Its entrance is cut into the hillside about 100 m from the cave's centre, on ground at least 10 m above sea level.
Each cave uses one of three layouts:

items: Fork and chamber: a central chamber with passages that branch off it.
Loop: two routes go around a solid rock mass and meet again.
Pillared hall: a broad, high hall held up by four rock pillars.

blocks.text: Floors climb in walkable half-metre steps. A cave ambience plays when you are under a roof.
Caves do not show on the map. Inside a cave there are no stalactites, dripstone, ores or lights.
Planned, not in the game yet: deeper cave networks, cave maps and dripstone caves.
Landmarks are rare sites about 220 to 320 m across. They do not form on water or lakes, on the ground within 512 m of the world's origin, or on very rugged ground. {{geological-landmarks}}
The ground decides which site you find:

items: Meteor crater: a bowl with a raised rim and two smaller craters beside it. Only on ground that is not volcanic.
Amethyst gorge: a winding canyon, 36 to 60 m wide and 24 to 54 m deep, through crystal-studded rock.
Lava tube: a walkable, roofed passage with two open skylights. Only on volcanic ground.
Geyser basin and hot-spring terraces: only on volcanic ground.
Cold uplands: ice spires, moraine ridges, outwash plains and firn domes.
Warm, wet ground: karst towers and tepui mesas. Warm, dry ground: spring oases.
Other ground: granite domes, limestone pavements and slate quarries.

blocks.text: Worlds made before the game recorded generator versions (Legacy worlds) have no landmark sites.
Sites are rare. Most of the map has none.

guides.title: Volcanoes, water and expedition sites
guides.headline:
Volcanoes, water and expedition sites
volcanic ground, the kinds of water, and the three finds.
guides.summary: Some islands have volcanoes of solid, cooled rock. Lakes, rivers, wetlands and hot springs each have their own kind of water. New worlds have three expedition sites with a one-time supply find.
guides.lead: This page covers the volcanic ground, the kinds of water you will find, and how to reach and collect the three expedition sites in a new world.

verification.method: Volcano shapes and ages come from crates/voxelgame-core/src/world/generator/relief.rs at Voxelgame 0494a0ce (volcano_plan, lines 172-195). Surface water kinds come from crates/voxelgame-core/src/world/generator.rs at the same commit (surface water material, lines 3666-3690), and the inland lake limit from MAX_INLAND_LAKE_LEVEL (sea level + 62 m, line 54). Block names come from crates/voxelgame-core/src/world/block/table.rs. Expedition placement, discovery, collection and find contents come from crates/voxelgame-core/src/game/exploration.rs in the same commit; the Journal labels come from crates/voxelgame-render/src/inventory_ui.rs.
verification.limits: Source-checked, not play-tested in this guide. A site is skipped when its square has no dry, level spot, so some new worlds may have fewer than three. The site squares are the code's rule; the exact site is somewhere inside its square. Source HEAD has moved past this pin, so the values here are from 0494a0ce.

blocks.text: Some islands have a volcano. Each one has one of three shapes. {{volcanoes}}

items: Shield volcano: a broad, low mountain.
Stratovolcano: a steeper cone.
Breached caldera: a summit crater with one side broken open. These are older and more worn down.

blocks.text: Older volcanoes are more eroded and more overgrown. Volcanic ground is made of basalt, obsidian, volcanic ash, lava rock, pahoehoe stone and magma stone.
Magma stone glows, but it does not heat you or set anything on fire. Steam vents and warm or boiling pools are found in the geothermal ground beside the volcanoes.
There is no molten lava and nothing burns. Steam vents are plain blocks: they do not make steam clouds. Flowing lava and fire are not in the game yet.
Islands have river channels, inland lakes, marshes, bogs, mangroves, bayous and frozen lakes. Inland lakes sit no higher than 62 m above sea level. {{rivers-lakes-wetlands}}
Natural water stays still. Rivers do not flow and do not push you. Water you place or dig out does flow.
The kind of water depends on where it is:

items: Ocean: Water.
Lakes and rivers: Fresh water.
Warm wetlands (marshes, bogs, mangroves and bayous): Black water.
Hot springs and geothermal ground: Hot spring water. The hottest pools are Boiling water.
Frozen lakes: Ice or Black ice. Frozen sea: Ice, Black ice or Glacier ice.

blocks.text: Boiling water and steam do not hurt you in this version.

Worlds made in the current generation (generation 10) have three small expedition sites near spawn. Each site is somewhere inside a square about 240 m wide. The three squares are centred about 215 m, 340 m and 440 m from spawn. The site ground must be dry and level. {{expedition-sites}}
Older worlds have no expedition sites. If the game cannot find a dry, level spot in a square, that site is missing.

items: Press E, then Tab to the Journal. The three sites are listed. A '?' means you have not found it yet, and a '+' means you have.
Click a site name to make it your destination. A beacon and an on-screen marker show the way.
Walk on the ground to within 12 m of the site. The status line says 'Discovered' and the site name.
Stay within 12 m, open the Journal and click Find next to the site. You must be on foot, not flying, sailing or riding.
Check that you have pack space. If you do not, the game says the find will wait there, so free some space and try again.
Survey workshop: 16 Alder boards and 8 Glass.
Reed refuge: 16 Reeds.
Stone overlook: 8 Chalk and 8 Basalt.

blocks.text: After you collect a find, its button reads Taken. Use Craft to turn the materials into buildings.
Each find can be collected only once, and the game saves that it was taken. Collect it before your pack is full; a find that does not fit waits at the site.

guides.title: Islands, biomes and world generations
guides.headline:
Islands and biomes
the endless sea, the 92 biomes and why old worlds keep their terrain.
guides.summary: A world is an endless sea of island groups. It has 92 named biomes, and each world keeps the terrain rules it was made with.
guides.lead: This page explains the shape of a world: the sea and its islands, the starting island, the biomes you can find, and why a saved world keeps its own terrain.

verification.method: Voxelgame a83e0c42, located by item name: crates/voxelgame-core/src/world/generator/archipelago.rs island tiers, atoll shape and fused cell pairs; world/generator.rs MIN_SATELLITE_STRAIT (240 m) and GeneratorVersion::Current = 10; Biome::ALL (92 entries) and generated_naturally() (true for every biome); game.rs with_seed (always Current) and save load restoring the saved generation; world/generator/terrain_profile.rs starting-island relief; crates/voxelgame-render/src/inventory_ui.rs Journal expedition text.
verification.limits: Source-checked, not play-tested. Island sizes are internal envelope values, so the tiers are described, not measured. The spawn point itself was not traced in code. Biome locations depend on the seed, so this page gives no map positions.

sections.title: The endless sea and its islands

blocks.text: A world is an endless sea. Island groups sit in it, and open ocean separates one group from the next. {{archipelago-and-starting-island}}

items: Small islets and palm-ringed atolls.
Regional and large islands.
Rare continent-sized landmasses.

blocks.text: A small islet sits at least 240 m of open water away from the main island it belongs to.
Your world begins on the starting island, at the origin (X 0, Z 0). Its terrain is gentler than the destination islands, and it is very unlikely to have a volcano.

A world has 92 named biomes. They range from meadows, orchards and bamboo thickets to salt flats, kelp forests, meteor fields and surface lava tubes. Every one of them can appear in a natural world. {{biomes-92}}
The map locator can find any of the 92 biomes, so you can travel to one you have not seen yet. See the maps guide for how to set a destination.

Each world keeps the terrain rules it was made with. Worlds made with Create world use generation 10. A saved world keeps its generation when it loads, so an update does not reshape land you have already built on. {{world-generation-version}}
No screen shows the generation number. The Journal's expedition section says "Landmarks appear in new generation-10 worlds" when your world is older.
A generation 1 world cannot contain meteor fields, surface lava tubes or amethyst gorges. To see them, create a new world.

guides.headline: Multiplayer and feature limits
guides.summary: LAN hosting, joining, saving on a server and recovering a stopped host, with the furniture and other limits that still apply.
guides.lead: Play together on your local network, then check the limits that still apply.
